title: Comprehensive Respiratory Set 1: Functional Anatomy (Short Answer)

questions.prompt: In the zero-to-23 generation model of the tracheobronchial tree, which generation is assigned to the trachea?.
What are the physiological roles of the conducting zone regarding the physical properties of inspired air?.
questions.modelAnswer: To warm, humidify, and filter the air..

questions.prompt: By what cellular mechanism do the conducting airways remove inhaled particles that bypass the nasal filters?.
questions.modelAnswer: Via the beating of cilia which sweep mucus-trapped particles upwards..

questions.prompt: At which specific generation of the airway does the "respiratory zone" begin?.
How is the anatomic dead space volume typically estimated for an adult based on their body weight?.
questions.modelAnswer: Approximately 1 millilitre per pound of body weight..

questions.prompt: According to the Bohr equation, how does the partial pressure of CO2  in mixed expired air compare to alveolar air when physiologic dead space is present?.
questions.modelAnswer: The partial pressure of CO2in expired air is lower than in alveolar air due to dilution by dead space air..

questions.prompt: Which three primary lung volumes must be summed to calculate the Vital Capacity?.
questions.modelAnswer: Tidal Volume (VT), Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV), and Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV)..

questions.prompt: Why is the Functional Residual Capacity (FRC) defined as the equilibrium volume of the combined lung-chest wall system?.
questions.modelAnswer: Because the inward collapsing force of the lungs is exactly balanced by the outward expanding force of the chest wall..

questions.prompt: Which specific lung volume remains in the lungs after a maximal expiratory effort and cannot be measured by simple spirometry?.
How does the calculation for Alveolar Ventilation (V˙A) differ from that of Minute Ventilation (V˙E ) in terms of "wasted" air?.
questions.modelAnswer: Alveolar Ventilation subtracts the dead space volume (VD) from each tidal volume (VT) before multiplying by the frequency..

questions.prompt: What is the definition of "Alveolar Dead Space," and in what clinical circumstance might it significantly increase?.
questions.modelAnswer: It refers to ventilated alveoli that do not participate in gas exchange, often due to a ventilation/perfusion defect like a pulmonary embolism..

questions.prompt: What is the approximate value for the partial pressure of CO2  in the anatomic dead space?.
Which alveolar cell type is responsible for the synthesis of dipalmitoyl phosphatidylcholine?.
What is the Respiratory Exchange Ratio (R), and what is its normal resting value?.
questions.modelAnswer: It is the ratio of CO2production to O2consumption, typically 0.8 at rest..
